title: One-Sentence Value Proposition Builder
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Entrepreneurship
description: Four dropdowns (Target Customer, Core Benefit, Founder Advantage, Main Alternative) each offer Jordan's wording, Priya's wording, or Write your own, which opens a text box. A preview card assembles '[Target Customer] gets [Core Benefit], from [Founder Advantage], unlike [Main Alternative].' live, wrapped to the screen, with each part in its own color. Formative feedback counts the parts filled in, estimates the read time against a ten-second goal, and flags missing parts, parts mixed from two founders, generic words, and sentences that run too long. Buttons load either founder's complete version or clear every choice.

prerequisites: Chapter 12 reading through The One-Sentence Value Proposition
educational.topic: One-sentence value proposition: composing target customer, core benefit, founder advantage, and main alternative into a single sentence a stranger can read in under ten seconds
learningObjectives: Compose a one-sentence value proposition by selecting or writing a target customer, core benefit, founder advantage, and main alternative
Revise the sentence until every part is specific and it reads in under ten seconds
Explain why every part of a value proposition must describe the same customer and offer

controls.label: Target Customer
controls.options: Jordan's wording, Priya's wording, Write your own; unset on load
controls.purpose: Choose who the value proposition is for

controls.label: Core Benefit
controls.options: Jordan's wording, Priya's wording, Write your own; unset on load

controls.options: Jordan's wording, Priya's wording, Write your own; unset on load
controls.purpose: Choose why this founder is the one to deliver it

controls.options: Jordan's wording, Priya's wording, Write your own; unset on load

controls.label: Clear

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Guided construction: deconstruct two worked examples, then build an original artifact from the same template with live formative feedback
keyQuestions: Which question does each part of the sentence answer for a stranger?
Why does a sentence that mixes Jordan's and Priya's parts stop describing a real business?
Which words in your sentence could any competitor also claim?
Can someone read your sentence in under ten seconds and repeat back what you offer?
commonMisconceptions: A value proposition should describe everyone who might buy, not one specific customer
Words like affordable or high quality make a value proposition stronger
A longer sentence with more detail is clearer to a stranger
assessmentOpportunities: Compose a complete sentence for one's own venture with no generic-word warning
Keep the sentence to 32 words or fewer (about 8 seconds to read)
Run the five-second test with a partner and revise from the result
